title: Posting and Applying Payments — Installment Payment Plans
content:
**Authorization of one-time payments — base clause, no longer in force as written.** The base sentence of the **Installment Payment Plans** "the customer personally authorizes each one-time payment taken by a representative, stating the card or bank account to be charged and the amount" is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis: for an endorsement deposit, for a returned-payment makeup and for a switch down payment, and only for such payments, the named insured authorizes the payment personally by running it with the representative, choosing the payment method and confirming the amount the representative states; every other one-time payment taken by a representative is authorized by the customer personally, stating the card or bank account to be charged and the amount. That authorization is the customer's own statement, not a system record.

**Single-payment cap.** A single card or bank payment may not exceed the plan's largest single payment (5000.00 on every plan).

**Order of application — base clause, no longer in force as written.** The base sentence "payments are applied in the payment application order: past-due invoices oldest first (fees before premium), then unpaid late and NSF fees, then the current invoice, then future installments nearest first; any excess is a credit" is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis: on a Monthly EFT or Monthly Card Autopay plan billing an Owner Auto Policy term, and only on such a plan, a payment is applied to past-due invoices oldest first (fees before premium), then to unpaid late and NSF fees, then to the current invoice, and whatever it leaves is held on the plan as a credit that its draft notices, or the first invoice after a move off automatic draft the named insured asks for, carry as their credit schedules set, an endorsement deposit and a switch down payment being held as their own schedules state; on any other plan, payments are applied in the payment application order, past-due invoices oldest first (fees before premium), then unpaid late and NSF fees, then the current invoice, then future installments nearest first, any excess being a credit.

**Posting.** A payment posts on the day it is received; a mailed payment also records its postmark date. A partial payment is accepted and applied in the same order. A personal check is refused on plans that do not accept personal checks (the Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan and the Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan).

**Agent-assisted payment fee.** The fee is charged only on a one-time payment taken through a live representative by phone, and it is the plan's agent-assisted payment fee. It is not charged on payments made online, through the automated phone line, by mail, at an agent office or by automatic draft; the payment's recorded channel is the evidence.

| Payment (hypothetical) | Agent-assisted fee |
|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan, card payment taken by a live representative by phone | 5.00 |
| same plan, same payment made on the online portal | none |
| Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan, payment taken by a live representative by phone | 0.00: the plan's fee is none |
| a card payment of 5,200.00 | above the 5000.00 cap; not accepted as one payment |

superseded_clauses: The customer personally authorizes each one-time payment taken by a representative, stating the card or bank account to be charged and the amount.

Payments are applied in payment_application_order: past-due invoices oldest first (fees before premium), then unpaid late and NSF fees, then the current invoice, then future installments nearest first; any excess is a credit.
